The Save America’s Rural Hospitals Act (H.R. 3684) claims to stabilize rural healthcare but fails to address the root problem: bureaucratic bloat. While it throws $25B at rural hospitals, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (H.R. 1) guts $58B from Medicaid—a net loss of $33B for rural providers. Connie’s concerns are valid, but Washington’s “solution” is robbing Peter to pay Paul.

Rural hospitals don’t need more temporary cash infusions; they need systemic reform to slash administrative waste, streamline Medicaid reimbursements, and end D.C.’s addiction to funding foreign aid over American communities.

Until Congress prioritizes efficiency over performative spending, rural healthcare will remain on life support.

@MartinHeinrich Banning terms like "climate change" and "emissions" isn't just censorship. It's a deliberate attempt to bury the truth and undermine the science that our communities rely on to survive.

The Energy Department isn’t censoring science—it’s cutting through bureaucratic jargon to prioritize results.
